subject: Production degradation post v4.2q rollout — executive escalation & rollback
messages:
From: Acme Retail Ops <ops@acme-retail.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@acme-retail.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in latency & errors since model-v4.2q rollout

Hannah —

We rolled the v4.2q variant to 100% at 08:45 PT and immediately saw p95 jump from ~120ms to ~520ms and p99 from ~320ms to ~1.6s. Error rate (502/timeout) increased to ~3.2% across our inference path. Attached are a small sample of the error logs and p99 graph (acme_p99_latency_20270918.png, acme_error_sample_0918.log).

This is impacting checkout flows and we’re seeing user-facing failures. Can you confirm whether this rollout changed any runtime config (qprofile, kernel selection) or if there are known regressions?

- Ops on-call
Acme Retail

Attachments: acme_p99_latency_20270918.png (image), acme_error_sample_0918.log (text)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Retail Ops <ops@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lena Park <lena.park@acme-retail.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in latency & errors since model-v4.2q rollout

Thanks for the quick heads up and the artifacts — we see the graphs. I’m escalating to engineering and CS now.

Immediate asks:
- Please hold any further traffic shaping changes on your side.
- Can you confirm the first request timestamp where you saw a 502 spike (UTC epoch or iso)?
- Are you able to divert a small percentage of traffic to v4.1q for comparison?

Irene, Aditya — looping you in, Acme hit p99 ~1.6s after our v4.2q push. The customer is asking for an immediate mitigation (rollback or canary).

I’ll coordinate the exec loop once we have a proposed short-term action.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
(Attachment: initial-ticket-ACME-78342.txt)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Acme Retail Ops <ops@acme-retail.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in latency & errors since model-v4.2q rollout

Hannah / team —

Prelim triage: we shipped v4.2q with an updated qprofile that selects the new int8-attn kernel on our A100 fleet. Early telemetry (internal perf traces) shows per-token decode time increased ~3x on hot paths for sequences >128 tokens due to an unintended kernel fallback when KV caching is populated. That fallback also produces a small but meaningful rate of malformed responses triggering 502s downstream.

Plan (proposed immediate actions):
1) Roll back serving config for Acme to v4.1q (previous qprofile) — fastest way to restore SLO.
2) Prepare hotfix that re-enables the optimized KV-cache path and add an additional integration test for long-sequence workloads.
3) Postmortem and credits discussion after stabilizing.

Aditya — can SRE prep the rollback_playbook_v1.md and runbook for an urgent rollback starting in the next 45–90 minutes? Marissa, please coordinate comms with Acme execs and confirm any contractual remediation we should offer immediately.

Irene Choi
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Marissa Cole

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Acme Retail Ops <ops@acme-retail.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in latency & errors since model-v4.2q rollout — diagnostic update

Team / Acme —

Quick diagnostic update from runtime traces we captured before and after the push:
- We observed an increase in KV-cache misses after the qprofile switch; the compiled runtime selected a slower attention kernel for cached sequences because a heuristic flag ended up disabled during the compile step for v4.2q.
- Error signatures in acme_error_sample_0918.log point to a short window where tokenization + attention kernel mismatch caused malformed token sequences and downstream 502s.
- Reproduced locally on an A100 replica with the customer's load shape; hotpath trace attached (acme_hotpath_traces.txt).

Given the impact, rollback remains the least risky immediate mitigation. If you prefer a hotfix deploy, it will likely take ~6–8 hours for testing and canarying before we reach parity.

Requesting decision: rollback now (recommended) or proceed with hotfix (longer).

Aditya Rao
Lead, Inference Performance
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Redwood Execs <execs@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive summary & remediation steps — Acme Retail (P0)

Team / Acme execs —

Executive summary: we acknowledge a production regression after the v4.2q variant rollout that elevated latency and error rates for your checkout flows. Immediate mitigation: we rolled back Acme’s production pool to v4.1q at 15:50 PT, and initial monitoring shows p99 trending back toward baseline over the last 10 minutes.

Next steps we’ve committed to now:
- Stabilize production for the next 48 hours and extend enhanced monitoring.
- Deliver a detailed root cause analysis and postmortem by EOD Tue (2027-09-21).
- Provide an account remediation: 30% credit for the impacted billing period; formal statement to follow from billing.
- Engineering will schedule the qprofile hotfix and additional validation in our CI for long-sequence workloads; we will not re-roll v4.2q to your pool until validated.

We regret the customer impact and will treat this as a high-priority remediation across serving runtime, compilation, and rollouts. I’ll schedule an exec sync if you’d like to go through technical tradeoffs or the postmortem draft.

Hannah Schmitt
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
(Attachments: acme_postrollback_snapshot.png)
